speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you had this wound on your right lower leg, and what were you doing when it first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the 10-year history of chronic swelling and family history, do you experience pain, heaviness, or visible varicose veins in that leg when you stand for long periods? Also, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or drainage from the wound recently? REQUEST TEST: Venous_Doppler_Ultrasound; REQUEST IMAGES: Lower_Leg_Photo.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Doppler Ultrasound Lower Limb: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg; Lower Leg Photo: Large ulcer on the right lower leg with discolored surrounding skin showing evidence of chronic changes and varicose veins.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer secondary to Chronic Venous Insufficiency.
